home.heroSubtitle: A lightweight resource pool scheduler with {scheduler}, {coolDown}, and explicit resource management.
home.heroVersion: Built on ES2024 explicit resource management with {dispose} / {asyncDispose}.
home.featureExplicitManagementDesc: Based on ES2024 {dispose}, resources are automatically released when leaving scope, preventing resource leaks.
home.featureSchedulerDesc: {Scheduler} automatically dispatches tasks to idle resources, supporting both {wrap} and {enqueue} calling styles.
home.featureCoolDownDesc: {CoolDown} callback controls the interval before a resource becomes available again after release, enabling rate limiting.
home.featureConfigDesc: Support factory functions, pre-created resources, custom concurrency, and async disposal.
home.featureZeroDepsDesc: Pure TypeScript implementation with no external dependencies, lightweight and ready to use.
home.featureAsyncDisposeDesc: {asyncDispose} waits for all resources to return before cleanup, ensuring complete lifecycle management.
home.ctaDesc: Learn how Pool.js works through the interactive Playground

examples.featuredDesc: An HTTP reverse proxy with concurrency control. Uses Pool.js Scheduler to limit concurrent requests to upstream servers, preventing overload.
examples.tutorial1Desc: Use {Scheduler} to limit upstream requests to a fixed concurrency. When the limit is reached, new requests queue and wait without overwhelming the target service.
examples.tutorial2Desc: Use {acquire} + {using} to implement automatic connection release, avoiding connection leaks.
examples.tutorial3Desc: Use {CoolDown} callback to control request frequency, avoiding being banned by target websites.
examples.ctaDesc: Start from the docs and quickly build your first project

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.overviewDesc: Pool.js is a lightweight resource pool scheduler built on ES2024 explicit resource management ({dispose} / {asyncDispose}). It provides an elegant way to manage limited resources (database connections, HTTP clients, Worker threads, etc.) allocation and recycling.
docs.overviewCorePool: Pool — Resource pool for managing resource creation, allocation, and recycling
docs.overviewCoreResourceContainer: ResourceContainer — Resource holder that manages the actual resource and its release
docs.overviewCoreScheduler: Scheduler — Task scheduler that automatically dispatches tasks to idle resources
docs.overviewCoreCoolDown: CoolDown — Callback to control the interval before a resource becomes available again
docs.poolDesc: {Pool} is the core class of the resource pool. It creates and manages resources, providing APIs for acquisition and scheduling.
docs.propConcurrencyDesc: Maximum concurrency, total number of resources the pool can manage
docs.propCreateDesc: Factory function to create resources, parameter is the current number of created resources
docs.propResourcesDesc: Pre-existing resource array, these resources are not destroyed when the pool is cleaned up
docs.propCoolDownDesc: Cooldown callback after resource release, controls when it becomes available again
docs.propShouldDisposeDesc: Whether to destroy created resources on pool cleanup (false when passing a resource array)
docs.acquireDesc: Acquire a resource from the pool, returns {ResourceContainer}.
docs.acquireDefaultBehavior: Default behavior: wait if no resource is available
docs.acquireNoWait: wait: false — throw NoResourceAvailableError immediately if no resource
docs.acquireContainerDesc: The returned {ResourceContainer} implements {dispose}, it's recommended to use the {using} keyword for lifecycle management:
docs.scheduleDesc: Create a {Scheduler} instance for task-based resource scheduling.
docs.enqueueDesc: Shortcut method, equivalent to pool.schedule().enqueue(). Directly enqueues a task.
docs.asyncDisposeDesc: Clean up the entire resource pool. Waits for all borrowed resources to return, then destroys pool-created resources and resets state. Recommended to use the {awaitUsing} keyword for automatic cleanup.
docs.asyncDisposeRecommended: Recommended: use await using keyword for automatic cleanup when leaving scope
docs.asyncDisposeAutoCleanup: Pool is automatically cleaned up after leaving scope
docs.resourceContainerDesc: {ResourceContainer} is the return value of {acquire}. It holds the actual resource and is responsible for releasing it when done.
docs.resourceContainerManualRelease: Manual release (usually not needed, recommended to use using keyword)
docs.withoutUsingDesc: If your runtime does not support ES2024 explicit resource management, or you prefer manual control, you can manage resource lifecycle by directly calling {dispose} and {asyncDispose}:
docs.withoutUsingNote: Without await using, manual cleanup is required
docs.recommendedPracticeDesc: Using {awaitUsing} and {using} keywords ensures resources are properly released even when exceptions occur, preventing resource leaks. If your environment supports it (Node.js 22+), always use {using} keyword.
docs.schedulerDesc: {Scheduler} provides task-based resource scheduling. You don't need to manually acquire and release resources — the Scheduler automatically executes tasks when resources are available.
docs.schedulerConcurrentTasks: All tasks run concurrently (limited by concurrency)
docs.schedulerEnqueueDesc: Enqueue a task. The task function receives pool resources via {this}.
docs.schedulerEnqueueAllDesc: Batch enqueue tasks, returns an array of all results. Accepts sync or async iterators.
docs.schedulerWrapDesc: Wraps a task function, returning a new function. When the new function is called, it automatically enqueues the task. Useful when reusing task logic.
docs.coolDownDesc: {CoolDown} is a callback executed after a resource is released. It receives resource scheduling timing information and returns a Promise to control when the resource can be allocated again.
docs.coolDownWaitDesc: Wait 100ms after resource release before it can be used again
docs.coolDownDeliverAt: Timestamp when resource was delivered to caller
docs.noResourceAvailableErrorDesc: Thrown when {acquire} is called and no resources are available.
docs.noResourceAvailableErrorLog: Pool is full, no resources available
docs.footerText: Pool.js v2 · Built on ES2024 Explicit Resource Management

playground.precreatedTooltip: Pre-created resources are not automatically destroyed
